programs.title: Governing the Algorithm: DAO Literacy for Worker Organizations
programs.grade_or_level: Adult continuing education / works council training
outcomes: Explain how an agent-managed, human-governed DAO differs from a traditional union structure
Identify which decisions must stay with people (final votes, charter changes, treasury) and which can be delegated to agents
Draft a sample workplace proposal for the Proposal Forum
Evaluate evidence summaries produced by agents for bargaining use

sessions.activity: Tour the charter, contribution model and measurable outcomes; compare reserved-for-humans decision lists with union bylaws on what members must vote on directly.
Read an Evidence Monitor summary; practice spotting missing context, sourcing and bias before using agent-written evidence at the bargaining table.
Work in small groups to draft a member-benefit proposal using the Proposal & Grant Drafter's template; peers debate while instructor plays steward holding final vote.
Use Progress Tracker dashboards to define measurable outcomes for a union campaign; discuss what metrics members would accept as fair.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized proposal drafts and rubric scores on agent-assisted drafting, so shared models can show which formats help worker bodies debate and decide fastest.
programs.consent: Adult participants sign an informed-consent form at enrollment; all contributions are pseudonymized, no workplace or employer identifiers are collected, and anyone can withdraw their data at any session.

programs.title: Crypto Valley Explorers: How a Town Governed by Lists and Lakes
outcomes: Locate Zug, Switzerland on a map and describe its lakeside old town and 'Crypto Valley' identity
Explain the idea of a ledger and why a shared record builds trust between strangers
Distinguish tasks agents can do from decisions only people should make
Design a simple class charter with reserved human decisions

sessions.activity: Map Zug's lake promenade and old town; then build a class 'charter' listing rules and marking which choices only the class may vote on, mirroring reserved-for-humans actions.
Sort fact cards about ledgers and DAOs into 'evidence' and 'opinion' piles; learn how the Evidence Monitor agent summarizes sources and where it can go wrong.
Teams draft a fun school-improvement proposal with help from a drafter role; classmates debate and hold the final vote themselves to see human governance in action.
Track the class charter's outcomes on a simple poster dashboard; each team reports progress and revises its proposal like the Progress Tracker agent would.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized, teacher-aggregated tallies of which proposal elements students found hardest to evaluate, used only to improve shared civics lesson materials; no student writing is shared.
programs.consent: Signed guardian/parent consent forms are collected before the module; only aggregate, anonymized counts are ever shared, no names or personal details are recorded, and guardians may opt out at any time without penalty.

programs.title: Evidence to Action: Running Agent-Assisted Program Cycles
programs.grade_or_level: Professional development for NGO program staff
outcomes: Map an NGO program cycle onto the five zones of an agent-managed DAO
Apply evidence-synthesis quality checks before adopting agent summaries into reports
Route tasks across working groups using an Operations Deck workflow
Define measurable outcomes aligned with a charter mission

sessions.activity: Compare the Evidence Monitor and Research Synthesis Agent roles; run a quality checklist (source, date, uncertainty) on a sample synthesis before citing it in program reporting.
Simulate the Task Router: teams triage a backlog of program tasks into working groups and time-box coordination between decision cycles.
Convert a field finding into a grant-style proposal draft; practice the human review gate where only stewards enact, agents never do.
Build an outcome tracker for one program indicator; agree what evidence would count as progress and who verifies it.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized cycle-time metrics (hours from task routing to human decision) and rubric scores on synthesis quality checks, contributed to shared benchmarks for agent-assisted program cycles.
programs.consent: Staff consent via organizational data-sharing agreement; individual contributions are de-identified, no beneficiary or community data enters shared models, and withdrawal is honored at any decision cycle.

programs.title: Charter-First Fundraising: Treasury Rules Humans Keep
programs.grade_or_level: Intermediate workshop for nonprofit leaders and boards
outcomes: Draft a charter-style mission with measurable outcomes for a small nonprofit
Understand why treasury transfers, enactments and appointments remain human-only
Use a Proposal Forum workflow to prepare board-ready grant drafts
Set up progress tracking that satisfies donor reporting

sessions.activity: Read the mission statement and contribution model; each leader drafts a one-page charter with mission, measurable outcomes and a reserved-for-humans decision list for their board.
Hands-on drafting: use the Proposal & Grant Drafter's structure to build a funding proposal, then run a mock board debate where only humans cast the final vote.
Design a task-routing board that splits volunteer and agent tasks between decision meetings; identify which coordinator roles the nonprofit still needs.
Translate the Progress Tracker approach into a donor-facing dashboard: pick three indicators and define the evidence trail behind each.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized charter templates and indicator definitions (never real donor or beneficiary data) so shared models can suggest which measurable outcomes nonprofit boards adopt most often.
programs.consent: Organizational consent letter plus per-leader opt-in; all shared materials are scrubbed of names, figures and locations, and any leader can remove their template from the shared pool at any time.
